newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: US sympathetic to Libya oil ban which remote at UN.
newsitem.headline: US sympathetic to Libya oil ban which remote at UN.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson said on Thursday he sympathized with Americans who wanted action on Libya, including an oil ban.
But he was non-commital on its chances of an oil embargo ever being adopted by the U.N. Security Council. Past U.S. efforts have failed and diplomats say such a ban is remote.
On Monday a bipartisan group of 53 senators sent a letter to Richardson, urging him to introduce a resolution to impose an oil embargo on Libya.

"I sympathize with their desire to find some means to make Libya respect the simple demands of justice," he told reporters. "We will continue to discuss with other council members ways to at least compel Libya to meet the justified demands of the Security Council," he said.

Libya has been subject to mandatory U.N. sanctions since 1992, including a ban on international flights and an arms embargo, for failing to extradite two men wanted by Britain and the United States. They are suspects in the 1988 midair bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, which killed 270 people.

The curbs were toughened in 1993 to include a freeze on some of Libya's assets abroad and a ban on its import of certain types of equipment used in oil terminals and refineries. They do not affect the export of oil from Libya or its purchase of oil-drilling equipment.
